chunks: As for the report which Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from one of the truthful ones, who said:

If a man is unable to obtain water but is able to obtain milk, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) with milk; rather, it is only water or tayammum. But if he is unable to obtain water and there is nabidh, then I heard Ḥarīz mention in a hadith that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had performed wudu (ablution) with nabidh when he was unable to obtain water.

So the first point concerning this report is that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah said, 'from one of the truthful ones,' and it is possible that the one to whom he attributed it was someone other than an Imam; even if he believed outwardly that he was truthful, acting upon it is not obligatory. The second is that the group has reached consensus that wudu (ablution) with nabidh is not permissible, so using it as proof also falls from this angle; and even if all of this were set aside, it would be interpreted as water flavored with a few dates cast into it when the water was bitter, so long as it had not reached a point that removed from it the application of the name 'water,' because nabidh in the language is that in which something is cast, and bitter water when a few dates are cast into it may be called nabidh; and this interpretation is indicated by that.

key_terms.التَّأْوِيلِ: interpretation reconciling the report with established legal principles
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: dry ablution used when water cannot be obtained
key_terms.اللَّبَنِ: milk, which is ruled invalid for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْعِصَابَةُ: the body of Shia scholars or transmitters whose consensus is cited
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the valid basis for ritual purification
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: ritual washing for purification before worship
key_terms.نَبِيذًا: a liquid infused by casting something into it; here discussed in relation to purification

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with milk or nabidh when water is unavailable?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling of purification when water is unavailable, stating that wudu (ablution) is not performed with milk and that the alternative is either water or tayammum. It then critiques a report about using nabidh for wudu (ablution), rejecting it on isnad and consensus grounds, and interpreting it—if accepted at all—as water lightly infused with dates without losing its identity as water.
